outroLine: How many did you get? Comment your score below, and subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!

lines.q: Fifty history questions, from easy to legend, and they get harder every round. Keep score! First one: which ancient people built the Parthenon?
lines.a: The Greeks! It was built in Athens to honour the goddess Athena.

lines.q: Who sailed across the Atlantic to the Americas in fourteen ninety two?
lines.a: Christopher Columbus! With just three small ships.

lines.q: Ancient Egyptians preserved their dead as what?
lines.a: Mummies! The whole process could take about seventy days.

lines.q: The Great Wall was built in which country?
lines.a: China! Measured with all its branches, it's over twenty one thousand kilometres long.

lines.q: Gladiators fought in the arenas of which civilisation?
lines.a: Ancient Rome! And most gladiators were slaves or prisoners of war, not volunteers.

lines.q: Nice start! Samurai were warriors from which country?
lines.a: Japan! The samurai class was abolished in the eighteen seventies.

lines.q: Where did the ancient Olympic Games begin?
lines.a: Greece! At Olympia, back in seven seventy six BC.

lines.q: Which Roman city was buried by Mount Vesuvius in seventy nine AD?
lines.a: Pompeii! The ash preserved whole streets, even loaves of bread.

lines.q: Who was killed on the Ides of March?
lines.a: Julius Caesar! The Ides of March is simply the fifteenth of March.

lines.q: Last one of round one. Where did the Vikings mainly come from?
lines.a: Scandinavia! Norway, Sweden and Denmark.

lines.q: Round two: medium, and it gets harder now. Which people built Chichen Itza in Mexico?
lines.a: The Maya! Its main pyramid has three hundred sixty five steps, one for each day of the year.

lines.q: Who ruled England when the Spanish Armada attacked in fifteen eighty eight?
lines.a: Elizabeth the First! Storms wrecked much of the Armada on its way home.

lines.q: Which English king had six wives?
lines.a: Henry the Eighth! Two of them were executed.

lines.q: What was the famous trade route linking China to Europe?
lines.a: The Silk Road! It was really a whole network of routes.

lines.q: Keep going! In which year did the French Revolution begin?
lines.a: Seventeen eighty nine! The storming of the Bastille is still celebrated every fourteenth of July.

lines.q: Who first printed with movable metal type in Europe?
lines.a: Johannes Gutenberg! His famous Bible came off the press in the fourteen fifties.

lines.q: Which Viking explorer reached North America around the year one thousand?
lines.a: Leif Erikson! A Viking site still survives in Newfoundland, Canada.

lines.q: In which century did the Black Death sweep across Europe?
lines.a: The fourteenth! It may have killed a third of all Europeans or more.

lines.q: Joan of Arc fought for which country?
lines.a: France! She was only about nineteen years old when she died.

lines.q: Last one of round two. Who founded the Mongol Empire?
lines.a: Genghis Khan! It became the largest connected land empire ever.

lines.q: Round three: hard. Ready? What was the capital of the Byzantine Empire?
lines.a: Constantinople! Today we call it Istanbul.

lines.q: Which Chinese emperor was buried with an army of clay soldiers?
lines.a: Qin Shi Huang! The first emperor of a united China.

lines.q: Suleiman the Magnificent ruled which empire?
lines.a: The Ottoman Empire! For forty six years.

lines.q: What did the Romans call London?
lines.a: Londinium! They founded it nearly two thousand years ago. Did that one get you?

lines.q: The legendary Hanging Gardens were said to be in which city?
lines.a: Babylon! Strangely, no one has ever found clear proof they existed. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: Whose expedition was the first to sail around the world?
lines.a: Magellan's! But he died on the way, and Juan Sebastián Elcano finished the trip.

lines.q: Halfway through round three! The ruins of ancient Troy are in which modern country?
lines.a: Turkey! Not Greece, as many people guess.

lines.q: Which people built the city of Tenochtitlan?
lines.a: The Aztecs! Mexico City is built right on top of it.

lines.q: Which general crossed the Alps with war elephants?
lines.a: Hannibal! The general from Carthage, in two hundred eighteen BC.

lines.q: Last one of round three. Who led the first team to reach the South Pole?
lines.a: Roald Amundsen! He beat Robert Scott by about five weeks.

lines.q: Round four: very hard. This is where scores drop. The houses of York and Lancaster fought in which war?
lines.a: The Wars of the Roses! A white rose for York, a red one for Lancaster.

lines.q: What was the first permanent English settlement in America, in sixteen oh seven?
lines.a: Jamestown! In Virginia, thirteen years before the Mayflower.

lines.q: The giant Colossus statue stood on which Greek island?
lines.a: Rhodes! An earthquake knocked it down after only about fifty four years.

lines.q: In which year is the Western Roman Empire said to have fallen?
lines.a: Four seventy six! The last emperor in the West was only a teenager.

lines.q: Still with me? What was the capital of the Inca Empire?
lines.a: Cusco! High in the Andes, about three thousand four hundred metres up.

lines.q: Which traveller wrote about the court of Kublai Khan?
lines.a: Marco Polo! He said he spent about seventeen years in China.

lines.q: Which ancient wonder was a giant lighthouse?
lines.a: The Pharos of Alexandria! One of the tallest buildings of the ancient world.

lines.q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India?
lines.a: Babur! In fifteen twenty six. His grandson was the famous Akbar.

lines.q: Which Chinese dynasty built most of the Great Wall we see today?
lines.a: The Ming! Most sections tourists walk on today are from the Ming era.

lines.q: Last one of round four. Which Greek city-state fought the famous stand at Thermopylae?
lines.a: Sparta! King Leonidas and his three hundred.

lines.q: Round five: legend. Only the best get these. Which emperor built the Hagia Sophia in five thirty seven?
lines.a: Justinian! For about a thousand years it was the biggest cathedral in the world.

lines.q: Which ancient people carved the city of Petra in Jordan?
lines.a: The Nabataeans! Right into rose red sandstone cliffs.

lines.q: Which peace treaty ended the Thirty Years' War in sixteen forty eight?
lines.a: The Peace of Westphalia! Signed in two towns, Münster and Osnabrück.

lines.q: Mansa Musa, maybe the richest man in history, ruled which empire?
lines.a: The Mali Empire! His pilgrimage to Mecca handed out so much gold it hit prices in Cairo.

lines.q: Which English king was executed in sixteen forty nine?
lines.a: Charles the First! England then went eleven years without a king.

lines.q: Which Roman emperor built a wall right across northern Britain?
lines.a: Hadrian! Building started around one twenty two AD.

lines.q: Which empire built Angkor Wat?
lines.a: The Khmer Empire! It's the largest religious monument on Earth.

lines.q: Three left, stay with me! Who invented cuneiform, one of the first writing systems?
lines.a: The Sumerians! They pressed it into wet clay more than five thousand years ago.

lines.q: Alexander the Great was king of which kingdom?
lines.a: Macedonia! And his teacher as a boy was Aristotle.

lines.q: Final question. In which year did Constantinople fall to the Ottomans?
lines.a: Fourteen fifty three! That ended the Byzantine Empire after more than a thousand years.

questions.q: Which ancient people built the **Parthenon**?
questions.fact: Built in Athens about 2,450 years ago to honour Athena.

questions.q: Who sailed to the Americas in **1492**?
questions.fact: He crossed with three ships: Niña, Pinta and Santa María.

questions.q: Ancient **Egyptians** preserved their dead as…?
questions.fact: Making a mummy could take around 70 days.

questions.q: The **Great Wall** was built in which country?
questions.fact: A 2012 survey measured all its parts at about 21,196 km.

questions.q: **Gladiators** fought in the arenas of…?
questions.fact: Most gladiators were slaves or prisoners of war.

questions.q: **Samurai** were warriors from which country?
questions.fact: Samurai were officially abolished in the 1870s.

questions.q: Where did the ancient **Olympic Games** begin?
questions.fact: The first recorded Games at Olympia date to 776 BC.

questions.q: Which city was buried by **Vesuvius** in 79 AD?
questions.fact: The ash preserved bread, graffiti and whole streets.

questions.q: Who was killed on the **Ides of March**?
questions.fact: The Ides of March is 15 March. Caesar died in 44 BC.

questions.q: The **Vikings** came mainly from…?
questions.fact: Vikings reached North America about 500 years before Columbus.

questions.q: Which people built **Chichen Itza**?
questions.fact: Its main pyramid has 365 steps – one for each day.

questions.q: Who ruled England when the **Armada** attacked?
questions.fact: The Spanish Armada sailed against England in 1588.

questions.q: Which English king had **six wives**?
questions.fact: Only two of his six wives were executed.

questions.q: What linked China to Europe for **trade**?
questions.fact: It was a network of routes, not a single road.

questions.q: In which year did the **French Revolution** begin?
questions.fact: It began with the storming of the Bastille on 14 July.

questions.q: Who printed with **movable metal type** in Europe?
questions.fact: His famous Bible was printed around the 1450s.

questions.q: Which Viking reached **North America** first?
questions.fact: A Viking site was found at L'Anse aux Meadows in Canada.

questions.q: In which century did the **Black Death** hit Europe?
questions.fact: It killed perhaps a third or more of Europe's people.

questions.q: **Joan of Arc** fought for which country?
questions.fact: She was only about 19 when she died in 1431.

questions.q: Who founded the **Mongol** Empire?
questions.fact: It became the largest connected land empire in history.

questions.q: What was the capital of the **Byzantine** Empire?
questions.fact: Today the city is called Istanbul.

questions.q: Which emperor was buried with a **clay army**?
questions.fact: The Terracotta Army has thousands of life-size soldiers.

questions.q: **Suleiman the Magnificent** ruled which empire?
questions.fact: He ruled for 46 years, from 1520 to 1566.

questions.q: What did the Romans call **London**?
questions.fact: Romans founded it around AD 47.

questions.q: The **Hanging Gardens** were said to be in…?
questions.fact: No one has ever found clear proof they existed.

questions.q: Whose expedition first sailed **around the world**?
questions.fact: Magellan died on the way; Elcano finished in 1522.

questions.q: The ruins of **Troy** are in which country?
questions.fact: Troy lies at Hisarlik, in northwest Turkey.

questions.q: Which people built **Tenochtitlan**?
questions.fact: Mexico City stands on its ruins today.

questions.q: Who crossed the **Alps** with elephants?
questions.fact: The Carthaginian general did it in 218 BC.

questions.q: Who first reached the **South Pole**?
questions.fact: Amundsen's team arrived on 14 December 1911.

questions.q: **York** and **Lancaster** fought in which war?
questions.fact: York had a white rose, Lancaster a red one.

questions.q: First lasting English **town** in America (1607)?
questions.fact: Jamestown, Virginia, was founded in 1607.

questions.q: The **Colossus** stood on which Greek island?
questions.fact: An earthquake toppled it after only about 54 years.

questions.q: In which year did the **Western Roman Empire** fall?
questions.fact: In 476 the last emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was removed.

questions.q: What was the capital of the **Inca** Empire?
questions.fact: Cusco sits about 3,400 m above sea level.

questions.q: Who wrote about the court of **Kublai Khan**?
questions.fact: He said he spent about 17 years in China.

questions.q: Which ancient wonder was a giant **lighthouse**?
questions.fact: The Pharos was among the tallest buildings of its time.

questions.q: Who founded the **Mughal** Empire in India?
questions.fact: Babur won the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

questions.q: Which dynasty built most of today's **Great Wall**?
questions.fact: Most sections tourists visit today are Ming-era.

questions.q: Which city-state fought at **Thermopylae** in 480 BC?
questions.fact: King Leonidas led the famous 300 Spartans.

questions.q: Which emperor built the **Hagia Sophia** in 537?
questions.fact: For about 1,000 years it was the largest cathedral.

questions.q: Which people carved **Petra** in Jordan?
questions.fact: Petra is carved straight into rose-red sandstone cliffs.

questions.q: Which peace ended the **Thirty Years' War**?
questions.fact: The Peace of Westphalia was signed in 1648.

questions.q: **Mansa Musa** ruled which empire?
questions.fact: His 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca was famous for its gold.

questions.q: Which English king was executed in **1649**?
questions.fact: England then had no king for 11 years.

questions.q: Which Roman emperor built a wall across **Britain**?

questions.fact: It's the largest religious monument in the world.

questions.q: **Alexander the Great** was king of…?
